ecological_or_specimen_meaning: Calendar alignment is retained across the measured series.
recognition_evidence: No persistent lag transition; edit counterfactuals provide no stable gain; reference cores agree on the baseline.

ecological_or_specimen_meaning: A locally absent or extremely narrow ring, often associated with suppressed cambial growth under drought, cold, fire or insect stress.
recognition_evidence: A unit negative step, a superior insert-year counterfactual and concordant gains against the master and independent cores.

ecological_or_specimen_meaning: An intra-annual density fluctuation or false boundary, including a ring divided twice during measurement.
recognition_evidence: A unit positive step, a superior delete-year counterfactual, residual support and consistent transition direction across references.

executable_edit: Move the older block by −q years
ecological_or_specimen_meaning: Localized decay, fracture, segment loss or a within-core measurement splice that displaces only part of the series.
recognition_evidence: One large local transition, a dominant range-shift counterfactual and agreement on the fixed-side breakpoint.

executable_edit: Move the complete series by g years
ecological_or_specimen_meaning: A negative shift is consistent with tree death, missing bark or sapwood, or a bark-side break that removed outer years.
recognition_evidence: Global sliding match, a constant lag path, terminal-side evidence and a whole-series counterfactual converge on the same g.

ecological_or_specimen_meaning: Several missing or false rings distributed through the series rather than one continuous displaced block.
recognition_evidence: Multiple intermediate lag plateaus, repeated unit counterfactual gains and stepwise recovery after each confirmed edit.

ecological_or_specimen_meaning: Nearby missing and false rings can cancel in long windows while retaining a distinct local disturbance signature.
recognition_evidence: Opposite local transitions, paired before/after evidence and matching votes on both sides of the short event interval.
